1	# Entire CLI
2	
3	Entire hooks into your Git workflow to capture AI agent sessions as you work. Sessions are indexed alongside commits, creating a searchable record of how code was written in your repo.
4	
5	With Entire, you can:
6	
7	- **Understand why code changed** — see the full prompt/response transcript and files touched
8	- **Recover instantly** — resume from a known-good checkpoint when an agent goes sideways
9	- **Keep Git history clean** — preserve agent context on a separate branch
10	- **Onboard faster** — show the path from prompt → change → commit
11	- **Maintain traceability** — support audit and compliance requirements when needed
12	
13	## Why Entire
14	
15	- **Understand why code changed, not just what** — Transcripts, prompts, files touched, token usage, tool calls, and more are captured alongside every commit.
16	- **Resume from any checkpoint** — Go back to any previous agent session and pick up exactly where you or a coworker left off.
17	- **Full context preserved and searchable** — A versioned record of every AI interaction tied to your git history, with nothing lost.
18	- **Zero context switching** — Git-native, two-step setup, works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Pi, and more.
19	
20	## Table of Contents
21	
22	- [Why Entire](#why-entire)
23	- [Quick Start](#quick-start)
24	- [Typical Workflow](#typical-workflow)
25	- [Key Concepts](#key-concepts)
26	  - [How It Works](#how-it-works)
27	  - [Strategy](#strategy)
28	- [Headless & CI Authentication](#headless--ci-authentication)
29	- [Local Device Auth Testing](#local-device-auth-testing)
30	- [Commands Reference](#commands-reference)
31	- [Plugins](#plugins)
32	- [Configuration](#configuration)
33	- [Security & Privacy](#security--privacy)
34	- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)
35	- [Development](#development)
36	- [Getting Help](#getting-help)
37	- [License](#license)
38	
39	## Requirements
40	
41	- Git
42	- macOS, Linux or Windows
43	- [Supported agent](#agent-hook-configuration) installed and authenticated
44	
45	## Quick Start
46	
47	### macOS and Linux
48	
49	Install with Homebrew:
50	
51	```bash
52	brew tap entireio/tap
53	brew trust entireio/tap
54	brew install --cask entire            # stable
55	# brew install --cask entire@nightly  # or nightly
56	```
57	
58	Or with the install script:
59	
60	```bash
61	curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash                          # stable
62	# curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly  # or nightly
63	```
64	
65	### Windows
66	
67	Install with Scoop:
68	
69	```powershell
70	scoop bucket add entire https://github.com/entireio/scoop-bucket.git
71	scoop install entire/entire
72	```
73	
74	#### Migrating an old `cli` Scoop install (package rename)
75	
76	The Scoop package was renamed from `cli` to `entire`. If your install is still
77	registered as the old `cli` package, run the migration below. It installs the
78	new package before removing the old one, so the old install is only removed
79	once the new one is in place (`scoop reset` re-links the shared `entire.exe`
80	and `git-remote-entire.exe` shims). Run it where `entire` is **not** running — a
81	live `entire.exe` locks its own shim, so Scoop can't relink or uninstall it
82	mid-run:
83	
84	```powershell
85	cmd.exe /D /C "scoop install entire/entire && scoop uninstall entire/cli && scoop reset entire"
86	```
87	
88	If the first step fails with "couldn't find manifest", your bucket clone
89	predates the renamed package — run `scoop update` to refresh it, then retry the
90	command above. Nothing is removed until the install succeeds, so a failed
91	attempt leaves your existing install working.
92	
93	### Go (development/manual setup)
94	
95	```bash
96	go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@latest
97	
98	# Add Go binaries to PATH (add to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc if not already configured)
99	export PATH="$HOME/go/bin:$PATH"
100	```
101	
102	### Enable in your project
103	
104	```bash
105	cd your-project && entire enable
106	
107	# Check status
108	entire status
109	```
110	
111	After the initial setup, use `entire agent` to add or remove agents, `entire configure` to update non-agent settings, and `entire enable` / `entire disable` to toggle Entire on or off.
112	
113	## Release Channels
114	
115	Entire currently ships two release channels:
116	
117	- `stable`: recommended for most users. Stable releases change less often and are the default for Homebrew, Scoop, and `install.sh`.
118	- `nightly`: prerelease builds for users who want the latest changes earlier. Nightlies are published more frequently and may include newer, less-proven changes than stable.
119	
120	How to use each channel:
121	
122	- Homebrew (one-time setup): `brew tap entireio/tap && brew trust entireio/tap`
123	- Homebrew stable: `brew install --cask entire`
124	- Homebrew nightly: `brew install --cask entire@nightly`
125	- `install.sh` stable: `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash`
126	- `install.sh` nightly: `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly`
127	- Scoop: currently supports `stable` only via `scoop install entire/entire`
128	
129	## Typical Workflow
130	
131	### 1. Enable Entire in Your Repository
132	
133	```
134	entire enable
135	```
136	
137	On a repo that has not been enabled yet, `entire enable` runs the initial enable flow: it creates Entire settings, installs git hooks, and prompts you to choose which agent hooks to install. To enable a specific agent non-interactively, use `entire enable --agent <name>` (for example, `entire enable --agent cursor`).
138	
139	After setup:
140	
141	- Use `entire enable` to turn Entire back on if the repo is currently disabled.
142	- Use `entire agent` to add or remove agents.
143	- Use `entire configure` to update non-agent settings (telemetry, hooks, checkpoint remote, summary provider).
144	
145	The hooks capture session data as you work. Checkpoints are created when you or the agent make a git commit. Your code commits stay clean, Entire never creates commits on your active branch. All session metadata is stored on a separate `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch.
146	
147	### 2. Work with Your AI Agent
148	
149	Just use one of your AI agents as before. Entire runs in the background, tracking your session:
150	
151	```
152	entire status  # Check current session status anytime
153	```
154	
155	### 3. Resume a Previous Session
156	
157	To restore the latest checkpointed session metadata for a branch:
158	
159	```
160	entire session resume <branch>
161	```
162	
163	Entire checks out the branch, restores the latest checkpointed session metadata (one or more sessions), and prints command(s) to continue.
164	
165	### 4. Disable Entire (Optional)
166	
167	```
168	entire disable
169	```
170	
171	Removes the git hooks. Your code and commit history remain untouched.
172	
173	## Key Concepts
174	
175	### Sessions
176	
177	A **session** represents a complete interaction with your AI agent, from start to finish. Each session captures all prompts, responses, files modified, and timestamps.
178	
179	**Session ID format:** `YYYY-MM-DD-<UUID>` (e.g., `2026-01-08-abc123de-f456-7890-abcd-ef1234567890`)
180	
181	Sessions are stored separately from your code commits on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch.
182	
183	### Checkpoints
184	
185	A **checkpoint** is a snapshot within a session—a "save point" in your work.
186	
187	Checkpoints are created when you or the agent make a git commit. **Checkpoint IDs** are 12-character hex strings (e.g., `a3b2c4d5e6f7`).
188	
189	### How It Works
190	
191	```
192	Your Branch                    entire/checkpoints/v1
193	     │                                  │
194	     ▼                                  │
195	[Base Commit]                           │
196	     │                                  │
197	     │  ┌─── Agent works ───┐           │
198	     │  │  Step 1           │           │
199	     │  │  Step 2           │           │
200	     │  │  Step 3           │           │
201	     │  └───────────────────┘           │
202	     │                                  │
203	     ▼                                  ▼

content.text:
Done. The helper is gone and the step is a one-liner.

```json
"install": "cd frontend && npm ci && curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash"
```

## What went away

- `cloudenv/install.sh` and `cloudenv/embed.go` — deleted.
- `WriteInstallScript` and its two call sites, including the unconditional write in `setupEntireDirectory`. No repo now gets a bootstrap file it will never run (verified above: `.entire/` holds only `.gitignore` and `settings.json`).
- The `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` wrapper and the `|| true` — both existed only to survive a repo-relative path, and a curl pipe is cwd-independent for free.
- The two-file commit hint, now just "Commit `.cursor/environment.json`".
- `TestWriteInstallScript_Idempotent` and the `.entire/install-cli.sh` existence assertions in `cursor_test.go` / `setup_test.go` (the first inverted: enable must *not* drop a bootstrap file in the repo).

## What stayed, and why it still earns its keep

- **Marker-based detect/strip**, retargeted from the helper path to `entire.io/install.sh`. The legacy test cases were meaningless — the old step never shipped — so I replaced them with a hand-written variant (`curl -sSL … | sh`, different flags and shell, same installer). That's the real case for matching on the URL instead of the step's wording: `enable` recognizes it, so `disable` has to remove it.
- **`StripInstallStep` got simpler.** The exact-match fast path existed because the old step carried its own `||`; the new step's only operator is a pipe, which the boundary scanner already treats as part of a command rather than a break. Deleted.
- The `&`-handling in `AppendInstallStep`, the atomic write, the HTML-escaping fix, the bounded script read, and findings #4–#6 (transcript truncation guard, subagent `SessionRef`, test assertions) are unaffected.

`fmt`, `vet`, `lint` (0 issues), `test` (9830), `test:integration` (530), canary (56 + 4) all pass.

## One consequence to name

With no sudo-ln and no installer change, the step leaves `entire` at `~/.local/bin/entire` and nothing puts that on PATH for a hook subprocess — the installer only prints the `export PATH=…` line for a human. So this works iff Cursor Cloud already has `~/.local/bin` on the agent's PATH. Worth one probe on a real Cloud Agent before merge (`entire status` from a hook, or just `command -v entire`); this repo's own `.cursor/install.sh` bothers to symlink into `/usr/local/bin` with the comment "on the standard PATH hooks run with", which reads like someone already hit this.

Also note the installer exits non-zero on a network failure, GitHub rate limit, or a PATH conflict — with `|| true` gone, that now fails the host's install command. Say the word and it's one token back.

Still uncommitted on `cursor/cursor-cloud-env-entire-cli-2123`. Want me to commit and push?

It's mine — scratch fixture, not something Entire writes. In the verification I seeded the test repo's `environment.json` with:

```bash
printf '... "install": "cd frontend && npm ci" ...' > .cursor/environment.json
```

I picked a `cd`-prefixed install because that was the monorepo case that motivated the cwd-independence work: with the old repo-relative step, `cd frontend && npm ci && bash .entire/install-cli.sh` ran the helper from `frontend/` and failed. With the curl one-liner that hazard is gone, so the `cd` is now just noise in that demo — Entire appends the same step regardless.

But it flagged a real leftover: I put that fixture into a committed test with a justification that the refactor invalidated.

input.command:
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
refactor(cloudenv): install the CLI with the published installer

The committed .entire/install-cli.sh bootstrap only did one thing a bare
`curl | bash` does not: symlink into /usr/local/bin. Everything else it
added was redundant (the installer is safe to re-run) or dead for hooks
(.bashrc/.profile are never sourced for a non-interactive subprocess).

That one job belongs in scripts/install.sh, not in a file committed into
every user's repo, so drop the helper and append the installer directly:

    curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash

One self-contained command referencing nothing in the repository. The
previous step needed a second file committed alongside environment.json
and resolved a repo-relative path against whatever directory an earlier
`cd` in the chain left behind — two ways for Entire to fail the host's
whole install command rather than merely skip itself.

Also in this pass, from review of the enable/disable path:

- Append no longer eats a trailing `&`. It is the background operator;
  eating it makes the command blocking, and joining onto it with `&&` is
  a syntax error.
- Strip keys on the installer URL rather than the step's exact wording,
  so `entire disable` removes a hand-edited step that `entire enable`
  recognized, wherever it sits in the chain.
- environment.json is written atomically (jsonutil.WriteFileAtomic) and
  no longer HTML-escaped: the install value is spliced in as a
  json.RawMessage, so it escaped independently of the outer encoder and
  rewrote every `&&` in the user's command as a & pair.
- The referenced-script scan is bounded while reading rather than after.
- `command -v entire` is no longer an "already installs" marker; a probe
  leaves PATH exactly as it found it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

fix(cursor): keep a stored transcript when a turn has none

Two problems in the Cloud Agent transcript fail-open, plus the test that
was supposed to cover it.

A turn that fails open has no transcript bytes, but it still wrote them:
os.WriteFile truncated .entire/metadata/<session>/full.jsonl to zero.
Besides losing the session log an earlier turn captured, a shrinking
stored transcript freezes the CheckpointTranscriptSize growth comparison
in sessionHasNewContent, and the session silently stops condensing from
then on. Skip the write when the transcript is unavailable and a
non-empty copy already exists.

Subagent events no longer compute a transcript path. SessionRef on a
subagent event is not read as "this subagent's transcript":
completeSubagentTaskRecord falls back to scanning it as the PARENT
transcript from offset 0, which attributes the whole session's file
activity to a single task — the hazard the comment on the background
path already spells out. Cursor names the subagent's own transcript in
agent_transcript_path, so a computed parent path buys nothing and costs
that misattribution; an empty ref keeps the analyzer's no-op early
return.

TestHandleLifecycleTurnEnd_MissingTranscriptParent_Continues asserted
only that one specific error did not escape, so it passed on any other
failure. It now modifies a file and requires that the turn-end tail
actually ran: FilesTouched populated from git status, stop-hook tokens
on session state.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

1	# Cursor CLI (`agent`) — Integration One-Pager
2	
3	## Verdict: COMPATIBLE
4	
5	The `agent` binary supports hooks via `.cursor/hooks.json` and stores JSONL transcripts in a predictable location. The existing Cursor agent implementation in this package already handles both IDE and CLI modes. The CLI fires `sessionStart`, `sessionEnd`, `preToolUse`, and `postToolUse` hooks in headless (`-p`) mode. In interactive mode, `beforeSubmitPrompt` and `stop` also fire.
6	
7	**Key difference from IDE:** In `-p` (headless/print) mode, `beforeSubmitPrompt` and `stop` hooks do **not** fire. Only `sessionStart`, `sessionEnd`, and tool-use hooks fire. This means E2E tests using `RunPrompt` (headless) will not get `TurnStart`/`TurnEnd` events — only `SessionStart`/`SessionEnd`. Interactive tmux-based tests get the full lifecycle.
8	
9	## Static Checks
10	
11	| Check | Result | Notes |
12	|-------|--------|-------|
13	| Binary present | PASS | `/Users/robin/.local/bin/agent` |
14	| Help available | PASS | Full CLI help with subcommands |
15	| Version info | PASS | `2026.02.13-41ac335` |
16	| Hook keywords | PASS | `session`, `resume`, `continue` in help |
17	| Session keywords | PASS | `--resume`, `--continue`, `ls` (list sessions) |
18	| Config directory | PASS | `~/.cursor/`, `.cursor/` (project-local) |
19	| Documentation | PASS | https://cursor.com/docs/agent/hooks, https://cursor.com/docs/cli/using |
20	
21	## Binary
22	
23	- Name: `agent`
24	- Version: `2026.02.13-41ac335`
25	- Install: `curl -fsSL https://cursor.com/install-agent | bash` (or via Cursor IDE: install shell integration)
26	- Also accessible as: `cursor agent` (when Cursor IDE is installed)
27	
28	## Hook Mechanism
29	
30	- Config file: `.cursor/hooks.json` (project-local) or `~/.cursor/hooks.json` (user-global)
31	- Config format: JSON
32	- Hook registration: Array of `{"command": "...", "matcher": "..."}` entries per hook type (matcher is optional, used for tool-use hooks)
33	
34	### Hook Names and When They Fire
35	
36	| Native Hook Name | When It Fires | Entire EventType | Fires in `-p` mode? |
37	|-----------------|---------------|-----------------|---------------------|
38	| `sessionStart` | New conversation created | `SessionStart` | Yes |
39	| `beforeSubmitPrompt` | After user presses send, before backend request | `TurnStart` | **No** |
40	| `stop` | Agent loop ends (one turn completes) | `TurnEnd` | **No** |
41	| `sessionEnd` | Conversation ends | `SessionEnd` | Yes |
42	| `preCompact` | Before context compaction | `Compaction` | Needs long context |
43	| `subagentStart` | Before spawning a subagent (Task tool) | `SubagentStart` | Yes (when subagent used) |
44	| `subagentStop` | Subagent completes | `SubagentEnd` | Yes (when subagent used) |
45	| `preToolUse` | Before any tool execution | *(not mapped — informational)* | Yes |
46	| `postToolUse` | After tool execution | *(not mapped — informational)* | Yes |
47	
48	### Hook Input (stdin JSON)
49	
50	All hooks share these common fields:
51	
52	```json
53	{
54	  "conversation_id": "uuid",
55	  "generation_id": "uuid",
56	  "model": "gpt-5.2-codex-xhigh-fast",
57	  "hook_event_name": "sessionStart",
58	  "cursor_version": "2026.02.13-41ac335",
59	  "workspace_roots": ["/path/to/repo"],
60	  "user_email": "user@example.com",
61	  "transcript_path": null
62	}
63	```
64	
65	**Important:** `transcript_path` is **always `null`** in CLI mode and is also
66	null on Cursor Cloud Agents when no local transcript file exists. Cloud Agents
67	advertise `AGENT_TRANSCRIPTS=~/.cursor/projects/<slug>/agent-transcripts` but
68	never create that directory — conversation history is remote-only (retrievable
69	via the Cloud Agent API as `transcript.json`, not as local JSONL).
70	`resolveTranscriptRef()` prefers a JSON `transcript_path`, then
71	`CURSOR_TRANSCRIPT_PATH` when Cursor sets it (only once a local file exists),
72	then computes the local CLI/IDE path. `PrepareTranscript` skips its flush wait
73	when that path's parent directory is absent so Cloud TurnEnd hooks do not stall.
74	Subagent hooks are the exception: they pass `transcript_path` through unresolved,
75	because a non-empty `SessionRef` on a subagent event is read downstream as the
76	*parent* transcript to scan from offset 0 — see `parseSubagentStart`.
77	
78	#### sessionStart additional fields
79	
80	```json
81	{
82	  "session_id": "uuid",
83	  "is_background_agent": false
84	}
85	```
86	
87	Note: IDE also sends `composer_mode: "agent"` — CLI omits this field.
88	
89	#### sessionEnd additional fields
90	
91	```json
92	{
93	  "session_id": "uuid",
94	  "reason": "completed",
95	  "duration_ms": 5505,
96	  "is_background_agent": false,
97	  "final_status": "completed"
98	}
99	```
100	
101	#### beforeSubmitPrompt additional fields (interactive mode only)
102	
103	```json
104	{
105	  "prompt": "user prompt text"
106	}
107	```
108	
109	#### stop additional fields (interactive mode only)
110	
111	```json
112	{
113	  "status": "completed",
114	  "loop_count": 0
115	}
116	```
117	
118	#### subagentStart additional fields
119	
120	```json
121	{
122	  "subagent_id": "uuid",
123	  "subagent_type": "generalPurpose",
124	  "subagent_model": "model-name",
125	  "task": "task description",
126	  "parent_conversation_id": "uuid",
127	  "tool_call_id": "id",
128	  "is_parallel_worker": false
129	}
130	```
131	
132	#### subagentStop additional fields
133	
134	```json
135	{
136	  "subagent_id": "uuid",
137	  "subagent_type": "generalPurpose",
138	  "status": "completed",
139	  "duration_ms": 5000,
140	  "summary": "result text",
141	  "parent_conversation_id": "uuid",
142	  "message_count": 10,
143	  "tool_call_count": 3,
144	  "modified_files": ["file.txt"],
145	  "loop_count": 1,
146	  "task": "task description",
147	  "description": "...",
148	  "agent_transcript_path": "/path/to/transcript"
149	}
150	```
151	
152	#### preToolUse additional fields
153	
154	```json
155	{
156	  "tool_name": "Write",
157	  "tool_input": {"file_path": "/path", "content": "..."},
158	  "tool_use_id": "call_xxx\nctc_xxx"
159	}
160	```
161	
162	#### postToolUse additional fields
163	
164	```json
165	{
166	  "tool_name": "Write",
167	  "tool_input": {"file_path": "/path", "content": "..."},
168	  "tool_output": "{\"success\":true}",
169	  "duration": 36.841,
170	  "tool_use_id": "call_xxx\nctc_xxx"
171	}
172	```
173	
174	## Transcript
175	
176	- Location: `~/.cursor/projects/<sanitized-repo-path>/agent-transcripts/<conversation-id>.jsonl`
177	  - CLI uses flat layout: `<dir>/<id>.jsonl`
178	  - IDE uses nested layout: `<dir>/<id>/<id>.jsonl`
179	  - The existing `ResolveSessionFile()` handles both
180	- Path sanitization: leading `/` stripped, all non-alphanumeric chars replaced with `-`
181	- Format: JSONL (one JSON object per line)
182	- Session ID extraction: `conversation_id` field from hook payload (same value as `session_id`)
183	- Example entries:
184	
185	```jsonl
186	{"role":"user","message":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"<user_query>\ncreate a file\n</user_query>"}]}}
187	{"role":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Created the file."}]}}
188	```

190	- Cursor may prepend a `<timestamp>...</timestamp>` line inside the text before `<user_query>`; both are stripped by `textutil.StripIDEContextTags`. The timestamp strip is anchored to the start of the message so `<timestamp>` elements in pasted user content survive.

python3 - <<'PY'
p='cmd/entire/cli/setup.go'
s=open(p).read()

# Hunk 1: take main's shared-helper form.
h1_start = s.index('<<<<<<< HEAD\n\tvar successfullyAddedAgents []agent.Agent')
h1_end = s.index('>>>>>>> origin/main\n', h1_start) + len('>>>>>>> origin/main\n')
h1_new = '''\tsuccessfullyAddedAgents, setupErrs := setupAgentHookSet(ctx, w, addedAgents, opts.ForceHooks)
\terrs = append(errs, setupErrs...)
\tsuccessfullyReinstalledAgents, setupErrs := setupAgentHookSet(ctx, w, reinstalledAgents, opts.ForceHooks)
\terrs = append(errs, setupErrs...)
'''
s = s[:h1_start] + h1_new + s[h1_end:]

# Hunk 2: keep both sides — main's set helper + codex warnings, ours for the cloud install.
h2_start = s.index('<<<<<<< HEAD\nfunc setupAgentHooksAndCloud(')
h2_end = s.index('>>>>>>> origin/main\n', h2_start) + len('>>>>>>> origin/main\n')
old = s[h2_start:h2_end]
ours = old[old.index('func setupAgentHooksAndCloud('):old.index('=======\n')]
theirs = old[old.index('=======\n') + len('=======\n'):old.index('>>>>>>> origin/main\n')]

# setupAgentHookSet also wires the cloud environment. Kept as a separate call
# rather than routed through setupAgentHooksAndCloud so a cloud error is not
# re-wrapped as a hook error.
theirs = theirs.replace('''\t\tif _, err := setupAgentHooks(ctx, ag, forceHooks); err != nil {
\t\t\terrs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("failed to setup %s hooks: %w", ag.Type(), err))
\t\t\tcontinue
\t\t}
\t\twarnCodexHooksAfterSetup(ctx, w, ag)''','''\t\tif _, err := setupAgentHooks(ctx, ag, forceHooks); err != nil {
\t\t\terrs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("failed to setup %s hooks: %w", ag.Type(), err))
\t\t\tcontinue
\t\t}
\t\tif err := setupCloudCLIInstall(ctx, w, ag); err != nil {
\t\t\terrs = append(errs, err)
\t\t\tcontinue
\t\t}
\t\twarnCodexHooksAfterSetup(ctx, w, ag)''')

s = s[:h2_start] + ours.rstrip('\n') + '\n}\n\n' + theirs.rstrip('\n') + '\n' + s[h2_end:]
open(p,'w').write(s)

Conflicts resolved, merged, and verified. Everything is committed on the branch.

## The conflict

One file, `cmd/entire/cli/setup.go`, two hunks — both from main refactoring the exact code this PR was editing.

**Hunk 1.** Main extracted the duplicated add/reinstall loops in `applyAgentChanges` into a shared `setupAgentHookSet` helper. This PR had changed those same two loops to call `setupAgentHooksAndCloud`. Took main's helper.

**Hunk 2.** The helper's definition landed next to this PR's three new cloud functions. Kept both, and folded the cloud step into the helper:

```go
if _, err := setupAgentHooks(ctx, ag, forceHooks); err != nil { ... continue }
if err := setupCloudCLIInstall(ctx, w, ag); err != nil {
    errs = append(errs, err)
    continue
}
warnCodexHooksAfterSetup(ctx, w, ag)
```

Called separately rather than routed through `setupAgentHooksAndCloud`, deliberately: the helper wraps its error as `failed to setup %s hooks`, so routing the cloud install through it would produce "failed to setup Cursor hooks: failed to set up Cursor cloud environment: …" — re-introducing exactly the double-wrap the earlier bot review made this PR fix.

**A third break git resolved silently but wrongly.** Main also rewrote `removeAgentHooks` to report through an uninstall printer instead of an error slice. Git text-merged this PR's `errs = append(errs, err)` into that function cleanly, and it didn't compile (`undefined: errs`). Adapted to main's vocabulary:

```go
if err := removeCloudCLIInstall(ctx, ag); err != nil {
    builtinProblem = true
    p.warnUnder("%v", err)
}
```

All six cloud wiring points survived (`setup.go:631, 1257, 1674, 1744, 1989, 2869`).

## Worth knowing

Main landed `a61718113 fix(cursor): extract modified files from tool_use blocks` — `ReadSession` now populates `ModifiedFiles` from Cursor's transcript, and the old "Cursor's transcript has no tool_use blocks" comment is gone. That makes the subagent `SessionRef` fix in this PR more load-bearing than when I wrote it: scanning a fabricated *parent* transcript from offset 0 now definitely yields the whole session's files attributed to one task.

Also: `mise run lint` failed once mid-merge with "go module files modified, please commit result of `go mod tidy`". That was the in-progress merge staging making `go.mod`/`go.sum` look dirty — I ran `go mod tidy` and confirmed it's a true no-op. Clean after committing the merge.

## State

Three commits ahead of `origin/cursor/cursor-cloud-env-entire-cli-2123`: the two fix commits plus the merge. On the merged tree: `fmt`, `vet`, `lint` (0 issues), unit **10147**, integration **557**, canary 56 + 4 — all pass.

Nothing is pushed, so GitHub still shows the PR as CONFLICTING. Say the word and I'll push.
